claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, do you have any children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have a son, Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions.

Since Alex is 17, I need to know: Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, or an approved training program)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not. He finished school but he's not doing any courses or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. I need to ask: Is Alex working, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services? (If he left education or training within the last 20 weeks and registered, you may still be eligible for that period.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have one more question:

Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent

conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

While you normally qualify for Child Benefit for children under 16 who live with you, Alex is 17 years old. For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can continue if they are under 20 **and** they stay in approved education or training.

Since Alex:
- Is not currently in approved education or training
- Has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services (which would allow Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks after leaving education)
- Is not in any approved training program

You do not qualify for Child Benefit for him at this time.

**However**, if Alex's circumstances change - for example, if he enrolls in college, starts an approved training course, or registers with a careers service - you may become eligible at that point. You would need to inform HMRC of any such changes.

For children aged 16 or over, you can still qualify if the child is under 20 AND they stay in approved education or training. Alex is not currently in approved education or training. The rules also provide an exception where Child Benefit can continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Alex has not registered with either of these services. Additionally, Alex is not working 24 hours or more per week and is not claiming benefits in his own right, but these factors alone do not make him eligible - he must be in approved education or training, or have registered with a careers service/armed services within the 20-week window. Since Alex is 17, not in approved education or training, and has not registered with a careers service or the armed services, the claimant does not qualify for Child Benefit for Alex.
